ChIJIwWTbKnj20ARm1tQRucQvT4.f45bdb1d043a:
Terrible.

Yesterday I came across an ad for a PR+ course on targeted advertising, where they promise to teach you — and I quote — "How to create Facebook Ads campaigns in one day and sell your products or services by the dozen."

According to them, the course is suitable for shop owners who ran ads but went into the red, for those whose targeting specialist got no results (meaning their course supposedly lets you run ads without a specialist), and — most interestingly — for those who've hit a ceiling on traffic, sales, and revenue.

Continuing. What you'll get from the course:

Daily 30-minute lessons
Ready-made packaged solutions
Online meetings and a personal mentor.

Additional bonuses:
Templates creation guide using AI
Ready-made audience templates
A service for editing ad creatives
A collection of 500 high-converting creatives

———
What they actually delivered:

Some mini-course called "Targeted Advertising" with lessons ranging from 3 to 7 minutes, covering content that isn't even beginner-level.

Just basic stuff — the kind of thing that's plastered all over the internet — like how to connect an ad account, how to link an Instagram page to Facebook, and other laughably common knowledge.

No daily 30-minute lessons.
No ready-made packaged solutions.
No AI template creation guide.
No ready-made audience templates.
None of the other things they promised in the course.

What there IS, however, is a questionnaire you're required to fill out before they'll even give you access to the product you already bought.

First of all — why should I have to do that?
I want to buy the product you presented and go through it.

How much I earn, what my ad budgets are, and everything else is none of your business.

I bought the course to take it — not to report back to you on what I do for work and how much I make.

Those questions would make sense if I were hiring you. But I just bought a course I want to take, and I have no idea why I should be handing over my personal financial information.

Second. Yesterday I happened to find another one of your courses first — one that caught my interest.

I bought it in the middle of the night. I hadn't even had a chance to look at it when your manager showed up in the morning with questions that had nothing to do with the course topic.

And started asking about projects, income, and everything else.

The manager who gave access to the targeting course launched into the exact same routine.

On top of that, he was asking for the same information already covered in the questionnaire.

Naturally, both in the questionnaire and with your managers, I gave information "off the top of my head" just to see what would happen next.

So it turns out that under the guise of a product you're peddling shockingly brazen nonsense — just to find clients, most likely to push your services on them.

Or possibly to sell them something else down the line.

When I asked my mentor — or whatever she is — why the course I was given access to doesn't match what you sell on your website, she said: because the course is still in development.

Could you please explain — what on earth possessed you to sell people a course that doesn't exist yet?

Your mentor didn't bother to mention that I'd bought a course that isn't ready yet. Didn't say anything like "just wait, you'll get access once we finish it."

She simply gave me access to a different product that has nothing to do with what I bought.

I have never seen anything like this anywhere. Do you really think your customers are that stupid?

I recommend neither the courses nor working with PR+ to anyone.

Looks like some office workers decided to move into the info-business.
